verified_signals.signal: Tatra banka operates 355 deposit-capable ATMs processing approximately 450,000 deposits per month. Limits: a technical cap of 200 notes per door-opening, which the bank has configured so a client can insert successive batches of 200 up to the depositor's/recipient's limit; no more than EUR 50,000 credited to one account or passbook per day; no more than EUR 10,000 deposited by one person. verified_signals.signal: Act 384/2025 Z.z. on the recording of sales took effect 01/01/2026, replacing the previous eKasa regime. Section 15 obliges every seller subject to sales recording to let the buyer pay cashlessly for any sale exceeding EUR 1 (exempt only where there is no internet signal or a failure of the confirmation technology). The as-published act set this from 01/03/2026; it was postponed to 01/05/2026 by indirect amendment Act 30/2026 Z.z. From 01/01/2026 the old positive annex listing which services must use eKasa is gone - the new act instead defines a short exemption list in Sec. 3(2) (severely disabled sole traders, high-mountain facilities without road/power connection, vending machines, supervised financial-market entities, and utility supply), so in practice all other service providers are captured. A third register type was introduced alongside the online and virtual registers: the 'softvérová on-line registračná pokladnica' (software online cash register), whose till program and protected data storage may be hosted in a remote/cloud environment. Sec. 3(4) requires a notice about the act's obligations at every point of sale, easily accessible and legible, with the template and placement rules set by the Financial Directorate (the widely reported A5 minimum size comes from that guidance, not from the act). PENALTIES, per Sec. 17: for the most serious eKasa breaches (Sec. 16 a-d, g, u - not using an eKasa register, disabling it, using a non-compliant register) EUR 1,500-20,000 on first detection and EUR 3,000-40,000 on each further detection; lesser breaches carry EUR 150-6,500 rising to EUR 300-13,000. For failing to enable cashless payment (Sec. 16 v): NO fine on first detection - the tax or customs office merely instructs the seller of the obligation - then EUR 500-15,000 on second detection and EUR 3,000-40,000 on each further detection. Serious breaches also trigger a sales ban at that point of sale of up to 72 hours and a referral to withdraw the trade licence.
verified_signals.source_name: Zbierka zakonov SR - Act 384/2025 Z.z. (official PDF, Slov-Lex)
verified_signals.implies: Every Slovak service business now needs an eKasa register AND a card-acceptance route, in force since 01/05/2026 - direct demand for Printec eKasa ECR, Android POS and acquiring enablement. The new cloud-hosted software register type is the format most likely to win the newly captured micro-merchants and is a software/SaaS play rather than a hardware one. The graduated penalty design (warning first, then fines) means the commercial urgency peaks at the second inspection, not the first.

verified_signals.verifier_note: I did not rely on the researcher's secondary source. I downloaded the official Zbierka zakonov PDF of Act 384/2025 from static.slov-lex.sk (32 pages), extracted the text and read Sec. 15, 16 and 17 directly. MATERIAL CORRECTION - the cashless-payment fine band was wrong. The researcher wrote 'cashless-payment breaches up to EUR 1,500 first and EUR 15,000 repeat'. Sec. 17(1)(h) actually reads: 'Sec. 16 pism. v) od 500 eur do 15 000 eur pri druhom zisteni porusenia; pri prvom zisteni porusenia podla Sec. 15 ods. 1 danovy urad alebo colny urad pokutu neulozi, ale predavajuceho pouci o povinnosti...' - i.e. no fine at all on first detection, EUR 500-15,000 on the second, and per Sec. 17(2)(a) EUR 3,000-40,000 on each further detection. CONFIRMED: the EUR 1,500-20,000 / EUR 3,000-40,000 eKasa bands (Sec. 17(1)(a) and 17(2)(a)) - but only for Sec. 16 a)-d), g), u); I added the lower bands so the claim is not overstated. CONFIRMED: 72-hour ban 'najviac vsak na 72 hodin' (Sec. 17(7)) and licence-withdrawal referral (Sec. 17(6)); Sec. 15(1) EUR 1 threshold and outage exemption; the software online register in Sec. 2(b)/(d) with remote hosting; the absence of a positive annex (only Sec. 3(2) exemptions); act effective 01/01/2026 (Cl. VIII). PARTIALLY CONFIRMED: the A5 notice - Sec. 3(4) mandates the notice but delegates the template and placement to the Financial Directorate, so A5 is guidance, not statute; corrected in the text. The postponement to 01/05/2026 is NOT in the published act (which says 1 March 2026); it was made by Act 30/2026 Z.z., which I confirmed via SKDP and Podnikajte but did not read in full - logged in residual gaps. Source upgraded from press (podnikajte.sk) to regulator (Zbierka zakonov).

verified_signals.signal: A preventive inspection campaign runs across four risk sectors - 'remeselne cinnosti v stavebnictve, starostlivost o telo, gastro a ubytovacie sluzby a sukromne zdravotnicke ambulancie' (construction trades, personal care, gastronomy and accommodation, private medical practices) - checking three things: that an eKasa register is present, that a cashless payment option is available, and that the statutory point-of-sale notice is displayed. Earlier enforcement: nearly 1,600 eKasa inspections in October 2025, about one third finding breaches, EUR 265,010 in fines; 222 inspections in the first twelve days of November 2025 with 48.65% finding breaches. Citizens can report a refused card payment to the Financial Administration.
verified_signals.implies: Enforcement is real, rising and now explicitly checks for a card-acceptance route - an urgency driver for POS/eKasa terminal sales to SME merchants, especially the newly captured trades and private-clinic segments that never had a register before. The published breach rates (one third to nearly one half) are the strongest sales argument available.
verified_signals.likelihood: High - campaign announced and prior-period statistics published
verified_signals.followup: Get the Financna sprava's own release with 2026 inspection statistics - the published numbers are all from Oct/Nov 2025 and predate the 01/05/2026 cashless obligation, so post-May enforcement intensity is unmeasured
verified_signals.verifier_note: Verified against the cited article, which resolves to an exact publication date of 11/05/2026 (the researcher recorded only '05/2026' - now precise). All four sectors, the three inspection checks, 'takmer 1 600 kontrol' in October 2025 with about a third in breach and EUR 265,010 of fines, '222 kontrol' in the first twelve days of November 2025 with 'takmer polovica (48,65 percenta)' in breach, and the citizen-reporting route are all present as stated. Caveat now recorded in the signal and followup: every hard statistic here is from 2025 and the article publishes no 2026 inspection data, so this is press reporting of past enforcement plus an announced campaign - the underlying Financna sprava releases were not retrieved.

verified_signals.signal: [STANDING - dated 2025] On 15/08/2025 Slovenska posta launched a five-branch pilot of self-service kiosks offering fast cash deposit and withdrawal, ePoukaz payment and Pay-by-square bill payment, payable in cash or by card, with no counter-staff assistance required. The pilot sites are Bratislava (Namestie SNP 35, and Mlynske nivy 5A - Stanica Nivy), Kosice (Humenska 4), Sturovo (Hlavna 60) and Zilina (Sladkovicova 14). The company said the project would be tested in real conditions and that its evaluation would determine how the concept develops further. As at 31/07/2026 no kiosk, self-service-terminal, ATM or cash-handling tender appears in Slovenska posta's public procurement record, and no public evaluation outcome or expansion announcement has been published; the authority's live 2026 procurements are a logistics information system (EUR 13,692,340 estimated, bids due 24/08/2026), security system support over 36 months (EUR 1,745,311), heating-plant operation, catering, cleaning and guarding.
verified_signals.source_name: SITA.sk (pilot announcement) / UVOstat - Slovenska posta contracting-authority profile (procurement check)
verified_signals.implies: Still pre-tender roughly a year after launch, so the window to shape specifications for a national post-office self-service kiosk rollout is in principle open - Printec's kiosk, cash-recycling and bill-payment stack fits the exact service set piloted. But nothing has moved publicly in twelve months, the pilot supplier is unknown, and 'no tender found' is absence of evidence, not evidence of absence: Slovenska posta also runs its own e-procurement portal (posta.eranet.sk) which could not be read.
verified_signals.likelihood: Low to Medium - a year-old five-site pilot with no published evaluation, tender or expansion decision
verified_signals.followup: Ask Slovenska posta directly for the pilot evaluation outcome and timetable; identify the incumbent kiosk supplier; monitor posta.eranet.sk and the UVO Vestnik for a kiosk notice
verified_signals.verifier_note: MATERIAL DATE CORRECTION. The researcher recorded source_date 31/07/2026, which was merely the access date and made a year-old pilot look current. The pilot announcement carries datePublished 2025-08-15T15:41:10+02:00 in the SITA page metadata, corroborated by the 24hod.sk syndication byline '15.8.2025 (SITA.sk)'. That is 11.5 months before this run, with no deadline, go-live or tender attached, so it is re-tagged [STANDING - dated 2025] and is_new flipped true -> false. The five branch locations and street addresses are confirmed verbatim ('Kiosky su v ramci pilotneho projektu rozmiestnene na piatich pobockach v mestach Bratislava (Namestie SNP 35 a Mlynske nivy 5A - Stanica Nivy), Kosice (Humenska 4), Sturovo (Hlavna 60) a Zilina (Sladkovicova 14)'), as are the service set and the 'evaluation will show how the concept develops' line. sita.sk returns 403 to WebFetch; I retrieved it with a desktop-UA curl and cross-checked the syndicated copy on 24hod.sk. The UVOstat procurement check is confirmed: no kiosk/self-service/ATM/cash tender in the 2026 list, logistics IS at EUR 13,692,340 with a 24/08/2026 deadline and security system support at EUR 1,745,311 both present as stated. OPP_SIZE downgraded L -> Unscoped: nothing about the scope of any rollout is evidenced, so any euro band would be invented. Confidence held at Low because the core forward-looking claim rests on an aggregator plus an absence of evidence.

residual_gaps:
ACCESS FAILURES (none silently dropped): (1) ce.asseco.com sits behind a Cloudflare interactive challenge - it returned 403 to WebFetch and to two desktop-UA curl attempts including full Sec-Fetch/Accept-Language/Upgrade-Insecure-Requests headers; all three Asseco pages (press release, ATM Multivendor product page, Referencie) were ultimately read via the Chrome browser tool, and the key figures were independently corroborated by two search-index snippets first. (2) finreport.sk and sita.sk both return 403 to WebFetch; both were retrieved with a desktop-UA curl, and sita.sk was additionally cross-checked against the 24hod.sk syndication. (3) The Slov-Lex consolidated HTML view of Act 384/2025 returned only page headers to WebFetch; I used the official Zbierka zakonov PDF from static.slov-lex.sk instead and parsed it locally. (4) posta.eranet.sk (Slovenska posta's own e-procurement portal) is a JS SPA and was not read - UVOstat was used as a proxy, so 'no kiosk tender' is absence of evidence only.

UNCLOSED VERIFICATION GAPS: (a) The postponement of the cashless-payment obligation from 01/03/2026 to 01/05/2026 was made by indirect amendment Act 30/2026 Z.z.; I confirmed its existence and effect via SKDP and Podnikajte but did not read the amending text or the consolidated Sec. 15 verbatim - the as-published Act 384/2025 still says 1 March 2026. (b) The Financial Directorate instruction that fixes the A5 minimum size of the point-of-sale notice was not retrieved; Sec. 3(4) only delegates the template. (c) No NBS or ECB payment-statistics cross-check was performed: the ~3,300 Slovak ATM count and the 45% contactless share rest solely on Asseco's own press release, which does not name its underlying data source, and the ~1,000 deposit-ATM figure is a Zive.sk calculation quoted by Finsider, not an official number. (d) SLSP's 2025 annual report was not consulted; the corrected ~300 recycler count rests on press reporting of the June 2026 event. SLSP's total ATM count is not stated by any 2026 source. (e) Tatra banka's and VUB's total ATM counts, and VUB's current (2026) deposit-ATM count, remain unknown - both banks' 2025 annual reports were not opened. (f) UniCredit SK's device count and its no-expansion stance are 18 months old and were not re-tested for 2026. (g) DanubePay (the second reference on Asseco's ATM product page, a Slovak card processor) was not researched at all.

NEW LEAD SURFACED DURING VERIFICATION, NOT YET VERIFIED (belongs to the next research pass, deliberately not added as a signal): Fio banka is building its own Slovak ATM network. FinReport (27/01/2025) quotes spokesman Jozef Dano saying deployment will continue into strategic locations across Slovak regions with a plan to reach 'minimalne 50 bankomatov v priebehu troch rokov' (at least 50 ATMs within three years) and an ambition to have a deposit ATM in every branch, with deposits possible via a digital wallet without a physical card. Related reporting exists at finreport.sk ('Fio banka na Slovensko prinasa vlastnu siet bankomatov') and sme.sk. This is a greenfield fleet build with a stated three-year horizon and was listed as 'remaining' by the original researcher.

CONFIDENCE DISCIPLINE: every signal is capped at Medium (one at Low); none was promoted. Twelve of the original twelve signals are kept - none was fabricated. Five carried figure, date or attribution errors that are now corrected in the signal text: SLSP recyclers 350 -> ~300; the cashless-payment fine band; the VUB 'territory-wide expansion' misattribution; the UniCredit growth framing (the source says expansion is NOT being prepared); and the Slovenska posta pilot date 31/07/2026 -> 15/08/2025. Four signals were re-tagged [STANDING] with is_new flipped to false (Asseco product page, Asseco reference list, the four unserved banks, Slovenska posta); the UniCredit signal was already correctly flagged is_new=false and is additionally tagged [STANDING].
